title: Critical Raw Materials Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1252
notes: Held as a record of what the act requires of a passport, not as a passport instrument. The word 'passport' occurs only in Art. 28(6), twice, and nowhere else in the Regulation:'For products referred to in paragraph 3 for which a product passport is required pursuant to another Union legal act, the information referred to in paragraph 4 shall be included in that product passport.' So the act creates no passport and displaces none, and it is not 'no passport' either: it owes content to the passport another act requires, which is what includedIn says. It was first filed as an act that defines a list of materials. Annexes I and II do supply the strategic and critical raw materials lists, which is why schema prose cites it, but Art. 28 is a disclosure duty. It binds a closed list of products: magnetic resonance imaging devices, wind energy generators, industrial robots, motor vehicles, light means of transport, cooling generators, heat pumps, electric motors including where integrated in other products (a motor there is one rated at 0,12 kW or more, Art. 2(47)), automatic washing machines, tumble driers, microwaves, vacuum cleaners and dishwashers. Art. 28(1): a conspicuous, legible, indelible label saying whether the product incorporates permanent magnets and of which of four types. Art. 28(3) and (4), where it does: a data carrier on or in the product, linked to a unique product identifier, giving access to the responsible person's name, trade name or trademark and postal address, each magnet's weight, location and chemical composition, the presence and type of coatings, glues and additives, and how to reach and remove every magnet safely. Art. 28(5) lets the magnet detail be replaced by the location and removal of the electric motors where the magnets are only in motors. Art. 28(7) puts accuracy and availability for at least the product's typical lifetime plus 10 years, including after an insolvency, on the person placing it on the market, at model level or, where units differ, batch or unit, open to repairers, recyclers, market surveillance and customs authorities. retentionYears is left unset because that period is relative to a lifetime and is not a number. Art. 28(8): where Union harmonisation legislation sets permanent-magnet recycling information requirements for a listed product, those apply in place of Art. 28. Art. 29 is a separate duty: a free-access website must show the recycled share of eight named elements where the magnets of types (i) to (iii) in a listed product weigh more than 0,2 kg. Art. 31 is not product content; it empowers footprint rules for the raw materials themselves. No product group in this catalog is on the Art. 28(1) list, so the instrument is deliberately unbound. The nearest case is Regulation (EU) 2026/1738, recorded with no vehicle group: motor vehicles are on the list, its vehicle passport must contain the Art. 11 information (Art. 13(2)(a)), Art. 11(1)(d) reaches parts and components containing what Art. 28(1)(b) refers to, and Annex VI point 2 lists the magnet types of e-drive motors. Its recital 37 calls those provisions the sector-specific implementation of the Critical Raw Materials Act while saying the Art. 28 labelling applies. Whether that displaces Art. 28(3) to (7) under Art. 28(8) is a legal reading this record does not make. Dates, as corrected: Art. 28(2) had the Commission adopt the labelling-format implementing act by 24 November 2025, not 2026 as first printed (Corrigendum 2024/90330), and Art. 28 applies two years after that act enters into force; from 24 May 2029 it applies to magnetic resonance imaging devices, motor vehicles and category L vehicles (Art. 28(10)). Art. 29(1) applies from 24 May 2027 or two years after its delegated act (due 24 May 2026), whichever is later, and Art. 29(6) gives those three product types five years from that act. Art. 28(12) empowers a delegated act listing Combined Nomenclature codes for the listed products. A Commission proposal to amend the Regulation, COM(2025) 946, would widen the Art. 28(1) list; it is a proposal and changes nothing recorded here. Text read: the Official Journal text of 3 May 2024 with Corrigenda 2024/90330 and 2024/90589. The consolidated text is the one to cite.
